_about: Prices and limits. Market prices drift 80-130% of 'market_base' each morning.
_about_balance: Tuned on 2026-11-15 for the 20-minute day (Alex: money should always feel meaningful and hard to get). Sweaters are the economy (Alex, 2026-11-15): every coin she earns comes from a sweater, sold to anyone in town face to face ('haggle'), to Rosa at the day's price, posted from the mailbox at the plain 'sell_prices' price, by mail order or for a local's request. Crops, wool and wild fibre can't be sold: crops are to eat, wool and fibre to knit. Jobs pay petty cash and drop something useful ('jobs' 'loot'). With two sheep and Gran's needles a day earns about 150c before rent, food and wool, so the first better needles take about three days. Every number is a draft.
_about_haggle: Selling a sweater to anyone in town (scripts/sweater_sale.gd; Alex, 2026-11-15). Asked once a day, a villager is looking for one with chance 'yes_base' plus 'yes_per_heart' for each heart and 'yes_per_trust' for each point of trust, or only 'rebuy_yes' if they bought one in the last 'rebuy_days' days. If they are, she sets a price: the meter shows how likely they are to say yes. Each villager has a hidden top price for the day, 'res_min'..'res_max' times the sweater's fair price (Rosa's price for its rarity) plus 'res_per_heart' for each heart; at it the chance is even, and 'spread' (a share of the fair price) sets how fast it falls off. An offer they turn down within 'counter_within' of their top price gets a counter-offer; after 'tries' refusals they walk away for the day. 'step' is the price buttons' step.
_about_wants: Which fibre a buyer asks for (scripts/sweater_sale.gd wanted_fibre(); Alex, 2026-11-24: 'request specific fiber types but nothing unobtainable ... requests scale as the game develops'). Each day each buyer face to face (the townsfolk with the red pin, a villager looking for one) wants a sweater knitted with one fibre, picked by 'weights' from the tiers open now: 'by_act' (the act -> the highest tier), plus one tier more once she has combed an animal of it (the Field Guide). 'plain' is sheep's wool (Game.sweater_fibres ''); the tiers are data/wildlife.json's. Before act1_done everyone wants plain wool (the guided first sale and Rowan's fourth task). Only a sweater of that fibre is offered. A local's request (data/requests.json) above the open tiers waits (empire.due()). 'value' multiplies the fair price face to face by the sweater's fibre tier, on top of 'rarity_price' (a fibre's knit_floor already lifts the rarity), so that at each fibre's floor a sweater is worth about: angora 1.6, fox or raccoon 3, beaver, coyote or mink 5, sable or lynx 10 and chinchilla 20 times a plain Common wool one (docs/REVIEW_2026-11-24.md section 5). Every number is a draft.

story._about: Act 1 (scripts/homestead.gd): Nora arrives with nothing; Gran's note leaves her 'gran_coins' (0 since 2026-11-16: she leaves her yarn and needles, and Wren buying the first sweater is the first money). Rent for Gran's house ('rent' coins every 'rent_days' days) goes in Gran's tin. Steve at Builder's Delight sells 'wood_pack' wood for 'wood_pack_price'. A fence panel takes 'fence_wood' wood; a gate is crafted (data/recipes.json). Max, her ex, visits the farm once she has played 'max_visit_hours' hours (main.gd _update_max_visit, data/scenes/max.scene). Lars, next door, rents her the barn for her animals: 'barn_rent' coins every 'barn_rent_days' days (a month), from the day her first sheep are penned; she pays him in person (homestead.gd).

marcus_house._about: Buying Marcus's house in Bretton Oaks (scripts/house_sale.gd; Alex, 2026-11-20): after his task (a hand-knit sweater, any, paid at its fair price) he offers it for `price` coins. Bought, she edits its walls, doors, windows and floors from Build & Buy while inside it, paid at "building"'s prices: a wall by the metre (half its 2 m `wall`), each opening at its `openings` price, a floor by the square metre (its `floors` price over four); half back for a piece she paid for and takes out, nothing for Marcus's own. A draft until Alex approves it.

shepherd._about: Rowan the shepherd (scripts/shepherd.gd; Alex, 2026-11-20): she can pay him to watch her pen. He costs `fee_share` of Lars's barn rent (data 'story' barn_rent) for `days` days, paid in advance on his menu, and is half as good as the barn: while he's paid up, each night the wolves come for animals the barn doesn't shelter he stops them with a chance of `cover` (rolled from the night, so the same night always rolls the same). Drafts until Alex approves them.

land.name: Greyspine Hollow
land.pitch: A stone cottage, a spring and a view of the whole range. The fog comes in like a postcard.

land.name: Saltmeadow Point
land.pitch: Sea on three sides. Sunsets you can sell tickets to. The crown jewel, and I don't say that about everything. I say it about most things.

_about_land: Gary's listings at Willow Homes (main.land_plots): shown on his menu and pitched on his visits to the farm (data/scenes/town.scene). Out of reach early on by design, and not for sale yet: buying land is still to come. Eastfield Acres left this list on 2026-11-24 to be the first large plot ("building" "plots"). Names, prices and pitches are drafts for Alex.
_about_building: Walls she builds in build mode (scripts/house_builder.gd; Alex, 2026-11-15): 'wall' and 'door' (a doorway) are coins a 2 m length, paid as each goes up. A room is about three days of sweater sales: a 4 x 4 m room against the house takes six walls (480c), the old 8 x 4 'Expand House' about 640c. Taking one down gives 'refund' of its price back. 'plots' are building plots Gary sells at Willow Homes ([x, z, width, depth], on the even grid), a little cheaper for each of his hearts; a plot with 'large': true is room for a town of her own (Alex, 2026-11-24): owning one in Act 2 or later opens Build & Buy's Town tab (build_plus.gd). Eastfield Acres, out in the Eastfield Meadows clear of Bretton Oaks, is the first, priced as about six days of mid-Act-2 takings (about 3,000c a day, docs/REVIEW_2026-11-24.md section 7); the first wall of a new house on one also pays 'new_house_fee' for the foundations. 'plot_sold' are Gary's lines. 'recolor' is what a new colour for a piece of furniture costs (data/furniture.json 'palettes'). Every number and line is a draft for Alex.

building._about_openings: Build mode's openings (house_builder.gd; Alex, 2026-11-17: every house's walls take doors and windows, for wood or coins), drafts: what each costs on top of a wall (a new wall with one pays both), in wood when she has enough for the whole thing, else coins. Taken out, half comes back in what was paid. 'door' is a plain doorway (its saved name).
building._about_stair_step: A step she adds to a flight in her Bretton Oaks house past Marcus's own count (house_sale.gd; Alex, 2026-11-23: the stairs set how high the floors are), a draft: wood when she has enough, else coins; taken out again, half back in what paid.
building._about_floors: Build mode's Floor tool (house_builder.gd; Alex, 2026-11-17), drafts: what one 2 m square of each floor costs, laid over a whole room at a click; wood when she has enough for the room, else coins; taken up (plank boards again), half back in what paid.
building._about_paint: Build mode's Paint tool (house_builder.gd; Alex, 2026-11-20: paint interior and exterior walls for a small coin cost), a draft: coins per 2 m of one side of a wall. Coins only, nothing back; no paint is free.
plot_sold: Sold! Lane's yours, or the brook's, I lose track. Mine says SOLD now either way. I'll have the lads clear it by morning. By this afternoon. By the time you get there.
Congratulations, you're a landowner. Foundations are on you, walls are on you, the view's on the house. Not literally. You'll need a house.

jobs._about_loot: Alex, 2026-11-15: jobs aren't for money. They pay a little petty cash and build the boss's familiarity and trust (requests come with hearts), and every full shift drops one thing from 'loot', picked by 'weight': 'item' goes in her bag ('n' is [least, most]); 'piece' is a piece of furniture she can place from the catalogue for nothing.
jobs._about: Jobs beside knitting (scripts/jobs.gd): petty cash, the boss's friendship and a random drop for a shift at someone's workplace. She holds one job at a time and works at most one shift a day. 'boss' offers it: the scene 'job_<id>' (data/scenes/jobs.scene) plays the first time she talks to them once the offer is due (after Act 1, and once their trust reaches 'trust' if given); if she says no, the boss's menu keeps a 'Take the job' row. She clocks in by talking to the boss between 'start' [from, to] o'clock. A shift walks her through 'tasks' 'rounds' times ('at' is where she stands and 'face' what she turns to, [x, z] in the 'building's own space, its front toward +z; 'secs' is how long each takes), or with 'round': true to every door in town. The clock moves on 'hours' over the shift, 'drain' comes off her needs spread over it, 'pay' coins at the end (part of it if she stops early), and a full shift adds 'perk' to her needs. 'lines' are what the boss says at the start and the end. Names, pay and lines are drafts for Alex.

bakery.name: Heart Bakery
bakery.perk_text: Giorgio sends you home with a warm loaf.

start: Apron's on the hook. Oven first, then the flour, then we'll see who comes in.
Six on the dot. Good. The dough noticed.
Wash your hands, cara. Then wash them again. Then bread.
done: Good work. Here, take this loaf. Don't argue, it's already wrapped.
You were quiet today. Quiet's fine. The bread came out right.
That's the morning. Go home, eat, sleep. In that order.

cafe.name: Cappuccino Cafe
cafe.perk_text: Sabrina slides you a coffee. 'It was going to waste. Probably.'

start: You're on the terrace. Don't drop anything. Or do, and I'll watch.
Tables one and two. That's all of them. Go.
Okay. Shift. Try to look like you like people.
done: You didn't break anything. Weird. Good weird.
Here's your money. Don't spend it on yarn. You will, though.
Same time tomorrow, if you want. I don't care. Come, though.

post.name: the post round
post.perk_text: Barbara tucks a peppermint into your pocket.

start: Here's your half of the bag, sweetheart. Every door, and a smile for whoever opens it.
Letters are lighter if you whistle. Try it.
Good shoes? Good. Off you go.
done: All delivered? That's a town that heard from someone today, thanks to you.
You walk like you're going somewhere now. That's new.
The round brings you back, sweetheart. It always does.

_about_store: Builder's Delight (Steve): her tools, seeds and wood over the counter (Alex, 2026-11-14: a new game starts with only Gran's shears). 'tools' is tool id -> price; 'seeds' is crop id -> [seeds in a packet, price]; 'seed_tin' is what Gran's seed tin on the kitchen counter holds. 'wool_packs_a_day' is how many packs of wool Rosa will sell her in one day, so her own animals matter.
_about_pastry: Heart Bakery's pastries (Giorgio; Alex, 2026-11-17): she buys them over his counter into her bag and eats one whenever she likes (click it on the hotbar when it's already in her hand, or press its number key again). Each gives 'energy', 'food' (her Hunger bar) and 'happiness' points out of 100. 'price' is before Giorgio's friendship discount (5% a heart). 'max' is how many her bag holds. The price is a draft.
_about_gear: What her money buys to knit better and go further (scripts/empire.gd; Alex, 2026-11-15). 'lantern': Steve's price for the lantern that lights her way at night. 'needles': better pairs, in order, sold by Rosa one step at a time; 'floor' is the least a sweater knitted with them can be (1 Common .. 5 Legendary). 'first_needles' is what she starts with. Names, prices and lines are drafts.

needles.name: Steel needles
needles.line: Steel, love. They don't bend and they don't snag. You'll feel the difference by the second row.

needles.name: Rosewood needles
needles.line: Rosewood. Warm in the hand. My own mother knitted with a pair just like these.

needles.name: Silver needles
needles.line: Silver. I've had these in the case eleven years waiting for someone good enough. Go on, they're yours.

_about_forage: Her axe and shears out in the world (scripts/forage.gd): a felled tree gives 'tree_wood' and grows back after 'tree_regrow_days'; a trimmed plant gives 'leaves' by kind (the start of its model name) and grows back after 'plant_regrow_days'. 'mulch_leaves' leaves mulch a growing bed, bringing it on by 'mulch_growth' of its whole growing time. Trees in Maple Grove itself aren't hers to fell.

bonfire._about: Bonfires (scripts/bonfire.gd, Alex 2026-11-17): she lights one on open ground from dusk (from_hour) to dawn for half a tree's wood (forage tree_wood 8 / 2). It burns until the next dawn. While one burns, midnight doesn't put her to sleep: the night goes on until morning. Within warm_radius metres her warmth heads for at least `warmth`; light_range is how far its light reaches; warm_up is what 'Warm up by the fire' gives. 'Sleep by the fire' sleeps her there till 6:00 like bed but gives back only sleep_rest energy (half a night's rest), so she needn't walk home to bed. Numbers are drafts.

fog._about: The fog over unexplored land (scripts/fog_of_war.gd, Alex 2026-11-17): everything outside a circle round the farm and Maple Grove (centre [x, z], radius, then fade metres to full fog) is under a light fog until she, or the dog she plays, has been within reveal metres of it. cell is the explored grid's cell in metres; top is the fog layer's height; density and max_alpha set how thick it looks (max_alpha < 1: you always see through it).

_about_build_prices: Build & Buy's prices for everything the world editor (god mode) can place that has no furniture.json entry of its own (Alex, 2026-11-24: "build mode near-identical to god mode but everything just has a coin price ... a tulip would be one coin ... repaving the ground a set amount of coin per square meter"). scripts/build_plus.gd reads it. "prefixes": the first whose start matches the model's name (a land's own kind, "swamp-rock_cluster", by its model, "rock_cluster") sets the price; "small" scales it for a "(small)" option; "default" for anything else. "shop_pieces": the price for a shop's or the café's own fittings, which have 0 in furniture.json. "ground": coins per square metre of ground painted with each surface, counted on the road map's own pixels (8 a metre), only where it changes. Taking a piece back up gives half its price back, as furniture does; the world's own scenery taken up gives nothing. Every price and label is a draft until Alex approves it.

build_prices._about_exclude: What Build & Buy never sells (Alex, 2026-11-24: "God mode's list includes odd things: yes, take out things that don't make sense"). god mode's own Place list keeps all of it. "exclude": Build & Buy ids ("w_<model>" for a world editor option, or a catalogue id), exact, or ending in * for every id that starts so: the crops and crop stages (she plants seeds), the tools, the knitting needles and the lantern as props (Steve and Rosa sell the real ones), the dog and the sheep (Lars sells real dogs, Rosa real sheep), the suitcase (a story prop), the plaza's cobble pieces (the Ground tool paints cobbles by the square metre) and the house editor's doors (the Walls row's Door tools put real ones in). The pieces still exist (a save that has one keeps it); they just aren't for sale. "prefer_scenery": where one model is in the catalogue twice (a catalogue piece and a world editor option, or a land's own copy of a kind), a model starting with one of these keeps the world editor's option at its scenery price (flowers, tufts, bushes, rocks, trees, hedges) and the catalogue's own piece is left out; any other model keeps the catalogue piece (the picket fence, the fountain).
build_prices._about_town: The town pieces (Alex, 2026-11-24: "I still want buildings and signs and mailbox as future options ... as I want the option to construct your own town from scratch. So anything town related we can have unlock when they purchase a plot of land."). "town" names them as "exclude" does: the town's buildings (the shops, the café, the Mayor's Office, the Bretton Oaks house), the barn, the bus, the shop signs, the welcome sign, the bakery stall and the post box (the market stall's model is the catalogue's Farm Stand, already for sale on her farm). They show in Build & Buy's Town tab (a draft name) only once Game.unlocked("town") (Act 2) and she owns a large plot ("building" "plots" with "large": true), and go down only on a large plot of hers (build_plus.gd town_open(), town_ok()). Set dressing for now: a building can't be walked into and has no shop, and a post box takes no post.
build_prices._about_names: Card names for pieces whose world-editor name reads oddly in the shop (Alex, 2026-11-24: rename "Building Bakery" and the like). Keyed by model; drafts.

acts._about: The four acts (scripts/acts.gd; Alex, 2026-11-24: Nora at 25, 50, 75 and 100, the skip hers to start once the act's last goal sets act_ready, everything she owns carried over). 'names' are each act's title on the skip's card (drafts). 'skip_days' is how far the calendar jumps (28: a season, so the weekday, the day of the season and every weekly sum stay where they were; the rent and other days still to come move with it). 'unlocks' is the act each later system opens in, read by Game.unlocked(name) (drafts: dogs, workers and her town at 2; mayor and shops at 3; the God Sweater at 4).

partners._about: Her partner (scripts/partners.gd; Alex, 2026-11-24: one partner at a time out of Rowan, Lars and Gary, never Max; boyfriend in Act 1, fiance in Act 2, husband in Acts 3 and 4; whoever she's closest to can take his place, which makes the men cross and leads to mild, silly sabotage). 'candidates' are the men who can be asked out (each also has "romance": true in villagers.json; Max is refused in code whatever this says). 'ask_at' is the romance a man needs before his menu has "Ask him out"; with a partner already, only the candidate with the most romance gets the row, and only once he leads the partner by 'switch_margin'. Switching makes the old partner sore for 'sore_days' days and takes 'sore_drop' off his romance; turning the new man down takes 'stay_drop' off his. While a man is sore: talking to him on 'mend_talk_days' different days, or any gift, ends it early; each talk has 'sharp_chance' of a sharp line instead of his usual one ('sharp'); each day there's 'argue_chance' that talking to him or her partner plays their argument (once per spell of soreness); and each morning there's 'prank_chance' of one prank, at most one every 'prank_every' days, from 'pranks' (only those that can happen: no pastry in her bag, no pastry prank). needles, itch and pen last until the next morning; pastry and paint until he isn't sore any more, when he puts it right. 'garish' is the paint he uses (house_builder.gd PAINT_COLOURS, not in the paint picker). 'titles' by act, 'lines' the toasts. Every number and line is a DRAFT until Alex approves it.

rowan: Sheep don't need company today. Neither do I.
lars: Oh. Hey. All good. Really. It's fine.
Radio's on. Can't really hear you. Sorry.
gary: Look who it is. Shouldn't you be with your {partner}?
I'd love to chat, but my hair has an appointment.
No, really, I'm thrilled for you. Can't you tell?

lines.pen: %s left the pen gate open, and one of your sheep has wandered out. Herd her back in.
lines.needles: %s hid your needles. You knit with Gran's spare pair today: one grade lower.
lines.itch: %s told %s your sweaters itch. They won't buy one today.
lines.pastry: %s ate a pastry out of your bag. Crumbs and all.
lines.paint: %s painted the front of your house a colour that can be seen from space.
lines.undo_pastry: %s left a fresh pastry by your door. Sorry, says the note.
lines.undo_paint: %s painted the front of your house back the way it was.
lines.itch_no: Someone told me your sweaters itch. Maybe another day.

dogs._about: More dogs (scripts/kennel.gd; Alex, 2026-11-24: 'purchasing additional dogs which you can use to hunt larger packs of animals at a time ... all the way up to 12 dogs maximum. Dogs are an expensive investment'; two animals per dog, data/wildlife.json herd_per_dog). Lars sells them from Act 2 (Game.unlocked('dogs')). 'max' counts her first dog too (so she can buy 11). The second dog costs 'price', and each after it 'price_mult' times the last, rounded to 'round' coins. docs/REVIEW_2026-11-24.md section 7 prices a dog at about 3 days of Act 2 income, which runs from about 1,000c to 10,000c a day: 3,000c is 3 days at the act's start, and at x1.26 the twelfth (the eleventh bought) is about 30,000c, 3 days at its end; all eleven come to about 120,000c. 'names' are given in turn to the dogs she buys, 'coats' in turn too (cream, red, chocolate, black, grey): 'tint' is the fur's colour (sRGB) in shaders/dog_scarf.gdshader, which keeps the fur's shading, and an optional 'model' per coat is for the breeds Alex will make (a GLB path; dog.glb until then). 'pack_bark_range' is how near the dog she plays a pack dog must be to bark when he does. 'lod_far' (metres from the camera) and 'lod_after' (the dogs past that many in the pack) think and animate at 'lod_hz' times a second instead of every frame. Every price and name is a draft until Alex approves it.
